scope: mechanical and isolated local-process verification; no live host acceptance

Duplicate launch intent is idempotent only for matching immutable bindings
Unknown launched process retains ownership and blocks duplicate admission
Secrets and raw authentication messages are excluded from durable traces
Foreign Core, provider and authority stores are never written
Actual bidirectional fixture process returns framed host records
Original finite deadline is preserved across commands and reconnect
Controller pipe loss terminates a TERM-resistant descendant with escalation
Normal leader exit cleans its descendant and does not claim model success
Inaccessible group identity retains uncertainty and capacity
Only the invocation-owned process group is signaled
Malformed, oversized or partial frames fail without manufacturing startup
Child environment is an exact whitelist with USER derived from uid
Codex startup requires actual correlated initialize/account/thread responses
Codex API-key, Bedrock, missing, different or changing account refuses
Claude startup requires actual intended-profile auth plus native init session/model
Harness readiness, caller UUID, generated text and replayed file refuse startup
Process start identity, native session, config digest, scope and attempt bind exactly
Expired source observation cannot issue a longer startup receipt
Unknown, extra or disabled guard configuration refuses model admission
Task context and effect tools remain unavailable during neutral initialization
Actual model identity remains unknown if the host never reports it
Reserve precedes resource preparation and real host initialization
Startup precedes provider In Progress confirmation and work lease
Provider failure or readback mismatch never grants model work
Every edit and command validates current attempt/session/deadline/resource ownership
Hold, revocation, rotation or changed attempt version prevents subsequent effects
Effect checks and execution use one controller serialization boundary
Only trusted exact command references are accepted; arbitrary shell argv refuses
Workspace read/write rejects escape, symlink, authority/config and foreign resources
Trusted command runner receives no provider credentials or authority mounts
Confined test runner edits/tests only the assigned fixture with finite limits
Runtime/model completion does not establish merge, deployment or human acceptance
Uncertain launch or teardown blocks competing attempts and retains evidence
Enrollment derives from owned authenticated host and exact provider principal
Caller-supplied grant/human/observer dataclasses cannot enter public tool APIs
Trusted foreground operator input binds exact scope/task/revision/destination
Model text or ASK request cannot manufacture human acceptance or hold release
Human instructions cannot widen scope or reopen delivered work without Core policy
Resume rotates the same logical capability and reloads its owned service
Stale host and service references fail after rotation
Partial reload stays fenced; restart reconciles intent without duplicate rotation
Disconnected unmanaged sessions cannot be silently enrolled
Queued context and cursor advance produce no delivered receipt
Actual bound host acceptance of event context establishes delivered only
Observed model tool request for exact event/challenge establishes AI acknowledgement
Caller event text, forged transcript and foreign native session do not acknowledge
Actual final public assistant output and accepted sink establish user report
Generated internal text or failed/disconnected sink leaves public report pending
All three stages require order and exact event/core session binding

Missing or untrusted native guards refuse supported admission
Native guard errors and unsupported tool paths do not become confirmed safe admission
Unknown host protocol version or configuration fields fail closed
Native tool observations never become product task authority
Package imports and host modules preserve the pure-Core dependency boundary
Existing runtime, process-group, scaffold and application regression suites remain compatible
